items.defectStatement: The eviction in add-buffer.lua can remove the segment/root payload when its end timestamp ranks among the oldest members, while leaving the has-root flag set. flush_segments then returns a segment without its root payload; done_flush_segments performs cleanup afterward.
obligations: Retain a payload whose span_id equals set_span_id whenever one exists before eviction.
Reduce the sorted set to at most 1000 members, evicting the oldest eligible members.
Preserve retained payload bytes, scores, and the set's expiration.
items.exampleFix:
if span_count > 1000 then
    local root_member = nil
    local root_score = nil
    local members = redis.call("zrange", set_key, 0, -1, "WITHSCORES")
    for i = 1, #members, 2 do
        if cjson.decode(members[i]).span_id == set_span_id then
            root_member = members[i]
            root_score = members[i + 1]
            break
        end
    end

    if root_member then
        redis.call("zrem", set_key, root_member)
    end
    redis.call("zpopmin", set_key, span_count - 1000)
    if root_member then
        redis.call("zadd", set_key, root_score, root_member)
    end
end
items.notes: The repository confirms that members are JSON payloads with a top-level span_id; the frozen input does not establish their encoding. The example protects one root representation, preserves its original score, and retains the cap. Merely clearing the has-root flag or deleting eviction does not satisfy these requirements.

items.defectStatement: Both ZUNIONSTORE calls use the default SUM aggregation, adding timestamp scores when the same payload exists in both input sets. The inflated score causes older duplicated spans to survive eviction ahead of newer spans.
obligations: Use non-additive score aggregation in both merges so identical timestamp scores remain unchanged.
Preserve merged membership, span_count assignment, merge conditions, and source-key cleanup.

items.defectStatement: Reducing the redirect loop's upper bound from 10000 to 1000 makes longer previously supported chains terminate at an intermediate ancestor. Subsequent redirects and merges can then place spans in the wrong buffer, splitting a segment.
obligations: Restore traversal capacity for redirect chains supported by the previous 10000 upper bound.
Preserve early termination on missing or self redirects and redirect_depth reporting.
Keep the traversal limit independent of the 1000-member eviction cap.
